title: H. G. Wells: The War of the Worlds — Ep 20/27 — "The Days of Imprisonment"
description:
The War of the Worlds, Episode 20. A fighting-machine arrives and fear drives the narrator and the curate into the scullery. Through the hole in the wall the narrator watches the Martians make metal in the pit, a tentacle placing a bright bar on the stack.

Starvation waits, yet the two men kick and thrust at each other over the peephole. The curate eats heavily and weeps for hours, and his muttering drives the narrator close to craziness. At dusk the pit glows green with aluminium fire, and a tentacle lifts a man from the cage against the stars. Then hooting begins, and the narrator runs into the darkness while the curate cries after him.

Next day the narrator weighs their chances. When the curate will not be quiet, he strikes him, ashamed, yet certain he would strike again. Days later he lifts the pantry door and digs with his hatchet, but the earth collapses and stops him.

Lying on the flags, he hears a booming far off: six reports, then six more in reply. The curate gives the closing beat: "Guns. Those were guns. Someone still fights them out there."

Chapter III of Book Two of H. G. Wells's The War of the Worlds (1898), "The Days of Imprisonment", in the public domain.

— The Keeper's Lantern —
Every episode is one whole chapter, in order, from the first page to the last.
